description_en: The temple is located within the religious complex of Dhuleśvara, on a hill 3,5 km north of Dullu.The site of Dhuleśvara is part of an area know as Pañcakośī. The sites of the Pañcakośī are visited by pilgrims from all over western Nepal. The sites are notorious for their flame temples (natural gas flames), said to mark places where Satī's body parts fell while Śiva carried her charred body (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009). While parts like the Satī's head (sirā) fell in Sīrasthān (DLK0130), the rest of the body, reduced to dust (dhūli), fell in Dhuleśvara.The monument is a freestanding temple with a square plan built on a stone and bricks platform. It has a door on each sides, the main one being oriented to the south. This main door is preceded on each side by wooden bell stands. The temple is covered by a hip slate roof. Inside the temple is a central circular cavity on which is a medieval stone model temple worshipped as aśivaliṅga(DLK0330-003). In front of the western door is a large stone disc (āmalaka) on which is a large stone statue of Nandi facing east (DLK0330-001). On the opposite side of the sanctum room is a lion statue facing east (DLK0330-002). These artefacts may be dated from c. 12th-16th century.The nearby Dhuleśvara Jvālā Ghar (DLK0331) is mentioned inSharma 2012, p. 93-95 andAndolfatto 2019, p. 177.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
